newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds inch higher, spreads idle.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds inch higher, spreads idle.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were slightly higher with Treasuries for most of a quiet session, following a long Easter holiday weekend.
Overall yield spreads to Treasuries remained largely unchanged, traders said.
"It's very quiet," one trader in New York said. "Everything is pretty much unchanged. If anything, (spreads) are a little bit on the tight side right now," he said.
By late afternoon, pass-through prices were flat to 2/32 higher overall, while comparable Treasuries were unchanged to 2/32 higher.
No major bid lists were spotted in the market, traders said.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons inched 1/32 higher at 100-15/32 bid, yielding 119 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 1/32 higher as well, at 100-15/32 and 100-21/32, respectively.
The five-year Treasury note was up 2/32 at 99-13/32 to yield 6.77 percent, while the 10-year Treasury note was up flat to yield 6.91 percent.
